title: Hidden in the Dark
sub: PreK–Kindergarten · Tomb Explorer · A painted wall from long ago

hero.credit: Facsimile by Nina de Garis Davies, 1924 · The Met

objective: Children will look closely at a wall painted in Egypt more than three thousand years ago, in the tomb of a man named Menna. With a torch, as in the exhibition’s *Tomb Explorer*, they will find a little cat, a crocodile and two big fish hidden in it, count, and say what the painting shows: a family in a boat on the river, among tall papyrus, birds and fish.

objectives.heading: By the end of this lesson you will be able to:
objectives.why: Long ago, a painter filled this wall with a family, a river and its animals. Looking slowly, a little at a time, lets us find what is hidden there.

items.text: find the little cat, the crocodile and the two big fish hidden in a painted wall
items.question: find what is hidden in the wall?

items.text: count the big fish on Menna’s spear, and say *two*
items.question: count the big fish?

items.text: say one thing the painting shows about a family in Egypt long ago
items.question: tell one thing the painting shows?

materials: A torch or flashlight, and a room you can darken
The marsh wall on page 3, printed large or projected
The differentiated handouts, one per child
questions: What can you see in the circle of light?
Can you find Menna? Can you find him twice?
How many big fish are on his spear? Let’s count.
Which animal is hiding in the water? Which one is at the top of the papyrus?
If you painted a wall about your family, what would you put on it?
connection: **Virtual visit:** open *Tomb Explorer* and choose *The marshes*. Turn on the torch and search for the crocodile, the little cat and the two big fish: when all three are found, the whole wall lights up.
**In the display case,** find the hand-crafted replica statue of Bastet, goddess of cats.

steps.title: A torch in the dark
script: Darken the room. Switch on a torch and move its circle of light slowly over the wall on page 3. Say: *“Long ago in Egypt, people made a special resting place for a person when they died, called a tomb. It is dark in the tomb. Its walls were painted more than three thousand years ago.”* Ask: *“What can you see in the circle of light?”* Let the children call out what they find before you show the whole wall.

screen.question: It is dark in the tomb. Shine a light. What can you find?

steps.purpose: Look before anyone explains: let the torch find the first details.

steps.title: Menna and his family
script: Turn the lights on and show the whole wall. *“This is Menna and his family, out on the river in a boat made of papyrus, a tall plant. On one side Menna throws a stick at the birds. On the other, he catches fish with a long spear.”* Menna is painted **twice** in one picture: let the children find him both times.
Ask: *“Who is in the boat with him? What is the water full of?”* The marsh is full of birds and fish.

steps.purpose: See the whole wall, and meet the family in it.
students: Find Menna. Can you find him twice?
Who is in the boat with him?

steps.title: What is hiding?
script: Now be detectives. A small cat climbs to the top of the papyrus, hoping to catch a bird. A crocodile swims in the water under the boats. And on Menna’s spear are **two** big fish. Children point to each one and hold up two fingers for the fish.

img.credit: Facsimile by Nina de Garis Davies, 1924 · The Met

screen.alt: A tomb painting: Menna stands twice in a papyrus boat among tall papyrus, on one side raising a throwstick at birds and on the other spearing fish, with his family beside him and water full of fish and birds below
screen.caption: A little cat, a crocodile and two big fish are hiding.

steps.purpose: Find the three details Tomb Explorer hides in this wall.
students: Point to the little cat at the top of the papyrus.
Find the crocodile in the water.
Count the big fish. Hold up your fingers.

steps.title: Your handout
script: Each child works on a handout. All three show pieces of the same wall, and the same hidden animals.

levels.name: Green Level
levels.summary: Picture-led. Circle the little cat, count the big fish and circle the number, find the crocodile in the water, then trace *CAT*.

levels.name: Yellow Level
levels.summary: Circle the cat, count the fish, find the crocodile, then copy *CAT* under a model and draw an animal to hide on their own wall.

levels.name: Red Level
levels.summary: Find all three in the whole wall, match each animal to where it lives, draw their own family in a boat, then tell a grown-up about it.

steps.purpose: Find, count and draw on paper, at the right level for each child.
students: Find the hidden animals on your page.

steps.title: Look back
script: Put the questions on the screen. For each one, the children show a thumb up, sideways or down: *“Can you now find what is hidden in the wall? Can you now count the big fish? Can you now tell one thing the painting shows?”*

screen.hint: Show me: thumb up, sideways or down.

steps.purpose: Check what each student can now do against the objectives.
students: find what is hidden in the wall?
tell one thing the painting shows?

steps.title: A cat and a goddess
script: Show the little cat beside Bastet. *“People in Egypt thought cats were very special. They told stories about a goddess of cats, called Bastet.”* Then ask: *“If you painted your own wall, which animal would you hide in it?”* Let each child whisper an animal to a partner.
